## Talks & Publications

Writing and speaking on amateur radio, digital modes, and the theory behind
them. I'm particularly interested in explaining *why* things work rather than
only how, and in finding the parallels between radio and other technical fields.

If you'd like me to speak to your club or group, contact details are in the
footer.

## Publications

### Understanding FT8 through DNA-sequencing parallels

**RadCom**, Radio Society of Great Britain, May 2026

FT8 routinely decodes stations at signal-to-noise ratios as low as −24 dB, on
bands that sound completely dead. My day job is with DNA sequencing systems,
which face a strikingly similar problem: reading billions of individually
minute, noise-swamped molecular signals at better than 99.9% accuracy. The two
fields arrived independently at the same engineering answers, namely structured
message formats, precise timing synchronisation, strong error correction, and
quality metrics.

The article uses those parallels to explain how FT8 achieves such extraordinary
weak-signal performance. No molecular biology or advanced mathematics required,
just the engineering trade-offs that make information transfer possible in
high-noise environments.

- [Blog post about the article](blog-posts/2026-04-25-ft8_dna_radcom.qmd)
- [RadCom](https://rsgb.org/main/publications-archives/radcom/)

### Seeing signals: I and Q from first principles

**RadCom**, Radio Society of Great Britain, September 2026

IQ data sits at the heart of every modern software-defined radio, yet it's
usually presented as an equation rather than something you can picture. This
article builds I and Q up from first principles and with minimal mathematics:
why a single measurement of a wave is ambiguous, how a pair of quadrature
measurements resolves that ambiguity completely, and what the resulting IQ plot
actually shows you for real signals, from a bare carrier and CW, through AM, FM
and SSB, to the digital modes.

A reader question about the article, on whether ASK, FSK and PSK can be
combined, is answered in
[Can you combine ASK, FSK and PSK?](thinking-posts/2026-08-16-combining-ask-fsk-psk/2026-08-16-combining-ask-fsk-psk.qmd).

Resources referenced in the article:

- [Setup for IQ visualisation and digital signal processing](guides-posts/2026-05-10-visualising-iq-setup/2026-05-10-visualising-iq-setup.qmd)
- [sdrconnect-iq-visualiser](https://github.com/IanHenry/sdrconnect-iq-visualiser),
  my SDRconnect IQ visualisation plugin
- [sdrplay-gnuradio-examples](https://github.com/IanHenry/sdrplay-gnuradio-examples),
  my GNU Radio flow graphs for SDRplay devices
- [SDRplay](https://www.sdrplay.com/) ·
  [GNU Radio](https://www.gnuradio.org/about/) ·
  [Radioconda](https://github.com/radioconda/radioconda-installer)

## Invited talks

### Understanding FT8 through DNA-sequencing parallels

**RSGB Convention 2026**, Saturday 10 October 2026

An invited convention session developing the themes of the May 2026 RadCom
article: why FT8 and modern DNA sequencing solve the same weak-signal problem in
the same ways, and what that tells us about digital mode design.

- [RSGB Convention speakers](https://rsgb.org/main/about-us/rsgb-convention/rsgb-2026-convention-speakers/)

### Making the invisible visible: understanding your SDR through IQ visualisation

**RSGB Convention 2026**, Saturday 10 October 2026

An invited convention session introducing IQ visually and with minimal
mathematics. It covers why IQ matters for modern radios, how to read an IQ plot,
and what analogue voice (AM, FM, SSB) and the digital data modes (CW, RTTY, FT8,
PSK, QAM) each look like in the IQ plane. It finishes with a live demonstration
using a purpose-built Raspberry Pi IQ visualiser.

- [RSGB Convention speakers](https://rsgb.org/main/about-us/rsgb-convention/rsgb-2026-convention-speakers/)
- [Raspberry Pi SDR](projects/raspberry-pi-sdr.qmd), the demonstration device

### Making the invisible visible: understanding SDR through IQ visualisation

[**Cambridge and District Amateur Radio Club (CDARC)**](https://www.cdarc.org.uk/),
8 May 2026

The first outing of the IQ talk, given to my home club. Starting from the idea
that a wave is the shadow of something rotating, it builds up to I and Q, then
works through what noise, carriers, CW, AM, FM, SSB and the digital modes each
look like on an IQ plot, with a live Raspberry Pi and RTL-SDR showing real
signals off air.

- [Raspberry Pi SDR](projects/raspberry-pi-sdr.qmd), the demonstration device
